name: New Hampshire
$scopeNote: New Hampshire has no tax on wages in 2025 either. New Hampshire has never taxed wages/salaries directly. Its only individual-income tax, the Interest & Dividends (I&D) Tax, was phased down (5% -> 4% for periods ending on/after 2023-12-31 -> 3% for periods ending on/after 2024-12-31) and fully repealed effective 2025-01-01 -- so 2026 is unambiguously a $0 year, not merely 'still phasing out.' No local income tax anywhere (New Hampshire does not permit municipalities to levy one -- towns/cities fund themselves through property tax instead). No employee-paid unemployment, disability, or mandatory paid-leave program: Granite State Paid Family Leave is explicitly VOLUNTARY (the nation's first state-sponsored voluntary plan) for both employers and employees, capped at $5/week for an individual buying coverage directly -- not a payroll tax with a fixed statewide rate the way NJ/NY/CT's mandatory PFML programs are, so not engine-consumed, same convention as Vermont's VT-FMLI.

reciprocity.note: Not applicable rather than 'checked, none found' — New Hampshire has no income tax to be reciprocal about, so no resident-vs-nonresident withholding question can arise here at all. reciprocalStates left structurally empty for consistency with every other state file's shape.

$yearNote: 2025 ruleset, built 2026-09-28 for prior-year corrections and retro pay. Only the fields the engine computes from were re-sourced for 2025 (suiEmployer). Descriptive fields (localIncomeTax.rule, reciprocity, paid-leave notes) are carried from the 2026 file; none of them changed between the two years.

knownGaps: Carried-over descriptive notes aside, this 2025 file models only employer unemployment (and, where the state has them, the employee unemployment, paid-leave, long-term-care and Seattle payroll-expense lines). Anything the 2026 file lists as unmodelled is unmodelled here too.
